findings.text: — the plan's prior-art sweep names seven heading walks (the `mcp_views._authored_section_headings` soup walk; the `_store.landed_section_ids` regex walk; the `_store` section-record attachment soup walk; the two `_store._require_new_section_contracts` before/after soup walks; the two `doccheck` soup walks that collect heading ids), and I confirmed that enumeration is exactly accurate for those seven sites — but the whole-package claim "The package today walks a plan's headings in seven places" is false.

— §16 says "one enumerator in `reckon/_store.py`" and claims section enumeration and extent "move to one home rather than gaining a third", but `reckon/_plan_html.py` already owns raw-text plan-span location: `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` yields per-heading identity and offsets in the same raw-text pass, and is already consumed for identity resolution (`reckon/_plan_html.py:890`) and for authored-text boundary protection (`reckon/_store.py:1644`). Building the enumerator on the `_H2_OPEN_RE` regex pair in `_store.py` adds a second raw-text scanner for the same question rather than extending the parser that already answers it, so after the change the package still carries two regex/raw-text span scanners and the "one home" claim holds only for the soup walks.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the change extends one owner (`plan_fingerprint` in `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`) to yield per-section digests behind the same name plus one coverage predicate, so one identity and one interface hide the section partitioning, the three identity forms and the landed-card exclusion.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 places a new raw-text section/heading enumerator in `reckon/_store.py` without citing `reckon/_plan_html.py`, whose `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` already scans raw text for per-heading identity and offsets and is already the owner of raw-text plan-span location.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1475, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 adds one public definition (the coverage predicate) and states in its own text that nothing is retired because the identity digest and the prose walk keep their names and gain a mode, and that the refusal reuses the existing plan-review-missing family rather than adding one.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the prior-art sweep enumerates seven heading walks and consolidates them, but omits `reckon/_plan_html.py`'s `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`, a raw-text h2/span scanner already in the package whose output is the same kind of (identity, offset) pair the new enumerator is built to yield.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the proposed enumerator replaces six callers of the existing walks rather than layering over them, and §16 states why the existing `_section_heading`/`_section_body_end` span pair is reused (the same scan the collapse derives its replaced span from).
